analytic.title: Node scaling scheduling of real-time tasks in a power-aware datacenter

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Power consumption of datacenters, especially of large-scale systems, has a growing concern nowadays due to economic and ecological reasons. In this paper, we propose a power-aware mechanism based on DVS that takes into account energy conservation of homogenous clusters and schedulability of deadline-constrained tasks. Although power-aware real-time scheduling heuristics have been intensively studied in the past decade years, they lack a theoretical guideline. From a theoretical perspective, we prove the necessary and sufficient conditions to test whether real-time tasks can be scheduled over a homogenous cluster, and deduce a lower bound for power reduction while guaranteeing the deadlines not violated. Besides, we develop the most power-efficient speed which can minimize the energy consumption. This speed is constant, only depending on the type of processor, and partitions an effective zone for speed scaling in a power-aware cluster. From a practical perspective, we propose a Node Scaling (NS) algorithm applying with other existing heuristics, which can further reduce the power consumption by extending the number of nodes and slowing the processor speed without missing any deadline constraints. Case studies are carried on Intel PXA270 processors. The simulation results show NS is effective for power reduction on the basis of EDF-FF.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Nowadays, a large number of new datacenters are being deployed all around the world due to the increasing demands of computing capability for big data. From the energy and environmental perspective, datacenters are the primary energy consumers, which constitute 2% of global total CO2 emissions and 3% of global energy consumption [1]. Therefore optimizing energy consumption in a datacenter becomes a key challenge for the development of the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) industry [2]. This paper studies a power-aware datacenter which can support real-time response to meet the requirements of deadlineconstrained applications.

A real-time application is a task with a sensitive deadline, a request of which must be responded to within a strict time constraint. Dynamic Voltage Scaling (DVS) techniques, known as one of the most effective approaches in reducing the power consumption of real-time systems, have been adopted by many previous researches to slow down the sys-tem when the workload is low [3]. With DVS techniques, the real-time scheduler with energy constraints should be able to guarantee the timing constraints of all tasks in the system and to select the speed of task execution so that the energy consumption of the system is minimized, or equivalently [4]. In this case, the problem is treated as an optimization problem that maximizes the optimality criteria (expressed as the total energy savings of the system) with feasible options [5], [6], [7], [8], [9]. Another approach considers idle time intervals on a feasible schedule. The actual number and length of these idle time intervals increase when some of the tasks run faster than their worst-case execution time. Therefore, the processor speed is dynamically adjusted to obtain a power saving when it is idle during a long interval [10], [11], [12].

Although power-aware real-time scheduling heuristics based on DVS techniques have been intensively studied in the past decade years, they lack a theoretical guideline to evaluate the power-saving performance. From a theoretical aspect, this paper proves the necessary and sufficient conditions to test whether real-time tasks can be scheduled over a homogenous cluster, and deduces a lower bound for power reduction while guaranteeing the deadlines not violated. The most power-efficient speed is proven which can minimize the energy consumption of the whole cluster. More interestingly, this speed only depends on the type of processor, and partitions an effective zone [(

Based on the theoretical conclusions, we propose a Node Scaling (NS) algorithm, which can be applied to other real-time heuristics. NS can further reduce the energy consumption by extending the number of nodes and slowing the processor speed without missing any deadline constraints.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 introduces the related works. Section 3 defines the problem, and Section 4 proves a power-efficient processor speed for minimizing power consumption of the whole cluster. Section 5 introduces a Node Scaling algorithm, and Section 6 evaluates its performance. Finally, concluding remarks are provided in Section 7. II. RELATED WORK Power-aware scheduling problems first attracted attentions from embedded systems which usually use only one DVS processor. Pillai et al. [11] proposed a mechanism to select the lowest possible operating frequency that allows the Rate Monotonic (RM) or Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling to meet all the deadlines. This frequency keeps static unless the task set is changed. Bini et al. [6] computed the optimal sequence of speed changes that minimizes power consumption while guaranteeing the feasibility of the schedule. Power-aware scheduling of real-time tasks in multiprocessor systems could be more energy-efficient than that in uniprocessor systems, due to the convex power consumption functions [8]. Aydin et al. [13] studied the problem of partitioning periodic real-time tasks in an identical multiprocessor cluster, and showed that the problem is NP-hard in the strong sense on 𝑚 ≥ 2 processors. Chen et al. [12] proposed a set of approximation algorithms for homogeneous multiprocessor systems. They proposed a polynomial time 2-approximation algorithm if the overheads in turning on/off a processor are negligible. Legout et al. [3] explored the trade-off between consumption reduction and deadline misses of the low-criticality tasks. They applied a mixed integer linear program to compute schedules that optimize the most efficient low-power states.

div.p: Although these approximation algorithms or heuristics can reduce power consumption, the time complexity is extremely considerable. Moreover, most of the researches in multiprocessor systems are practical-oriented, and they lack a theoretical analysis on the general scheduling problem. In this paper, we build a theoretical model of power reduction based on DVS technology, and prove an effective zone for scaling processor speed, which is useful for choosing the most power-efficient speed to guarantee the schedulability of a given task set. div.head: III. PROBLEM STATEMENT A. Homogeneous Cluster
div.p: In this paper, we will consider the hard-real-time scheduling problem upon a homogeneous cluster comprised of 𝑚 processors with DVS techniques. In the homogeneous cluster, all processors are identical in the sense that they have the same computing speed and power consumption. Each processor is characterized by a single parameter 𝑠, which is the frequency of processor in [𝑠 𝑚𝑖𝑛 , 𝑠 𝑚𝑎𝑥 ]. The cluster is represented as 𝜋 = [𝑠 1 , 𝑠 2 , . . . , 𝑠 𝑚 ], and 𝑆 𝑚 = ∑ 𝑚 𝑖=1 𝑠 𝑖 = 𝑚𝑠 shows the computing capability of the whole cluster.

The power consumption of one processor is represented through speed (frequency) and voltage. For a DVS processor, the power consumption function 𝑃 consists of 2 parts: a static part existing even when there is no workload (due to the leakage) and a dynamic part which is related to speed [14] .

div.head: B. Real-time Tasks
div.p: Real-time scheduling usually classifies tasks into periodic, aperiodic and sporadic. Among them, the periodic task model is widely studied for analyzing real-time processing systems. In this paper, we suppose that tasks are periodic and independent. The task set to be scheduled is represented as 𝜏 = {𝑇 1 , 𝑇 2 , . . . , 𝑇 𝑛 }. A periodic task 𝑇 𝑖 consists of a sequence of real-time jobs semantically related 𝑇 𝑖 = (𝐽 1 𝑖 , 𝐽 2 𝑖 , . . . ). For any 1 ≤ 𝑗 < 𝑘, the request time of 𝐽 𝑗 𝑖 is earlier than the request time of 𝐽 𝑘 𝑖 . 𝑇 𝑖 can also be denoted by (𝑐 𝑖 , 𝑝 𝑖 ), where 𝑐 𝑖 is the execution requirement in CPU cycles and 𝑝 𝑖 is the period. 𝐽 𝑘 𝑖 arrives at (𝑘 -1)𝑝 𝑖 and must complete before 𝑘𝑝 𝑖 . Here 𝑝 𝑖 can be considered as the strict deadline for 𝐽 𝑘 𝑖 . If any job in 𝑇 𝑖 misses the deadline, 𝑇 𝑖 turns to be a failed task. The utilization 𝑢 𝑖 of task 𝑇 𝑖 is defined as the ratio of its execution requirement to its period, 𝑢 𝑖 = 𝑐 𝑖 /𝑝 𝑖 . The set utilization 𝑈 𝑛 is defined as 𝑈 𝑛 = ∑ 𝑛 𝑖=1 𝑢 𝑖 .

div.head: C. Scheduling Algorithms
div.p: Multiprocessor scheduling includes two parts: a reasonable allocation algorithm which allocates tasks to processors and a uniprocessor scheduling algorithm which decides the sequence of job execution in a single processor based on job priority. An example for uniprocessor algorithm is the well-known RM algorithm or EDF algorithm. First Fit (FF), Best Fit (BF) or Worst Fit (WF) heuristics are examples of reasonable allocation algorithm. In this paper, a scheduling algorithm is represented as a pair of an uniprocessor scheduling algorithm and a reasonable allocation algorithm, such as EDF-FF.

div.head: D. Optimization Objective
div.p: Given a set of real-time tasks 𝜏 = {𝑇 1 , 𝑇 2 , . . . , 𝑇 𝑛 }, we attempt to determine the most power-efficient state of homogenous cluster 𝜋 = [𝑠 1 , 𝑠 2 , . . . , 𝑠 𝑚 ]. To be more specific, the state mainly contains two parameters: the cluster size 𝑚 and the processor speed 𝑠. These processors can guarantee the deadlines of the tasks not violated while minimizing power consumption for the whole system.

div.head: IV. POWER-AWARE SCHEDULABILITY TEST
div.p: Schedulability test is used to predict temporal behavior of a given task set. It can decide whether the deadline constraints will be meet in advance, that is, the given task set can be scheduled. Exact schedulability test yields to sufficient and necessary condition. Audsley [15] proposed an exact schedulability test by searching worst-case response time in an iterative manner. Funk et al. [16] studied the problem of exact schedulability test for determining whether a given periodic task set is schedulable on a particular uniform multiprocessor system. Since an homogenous cluster can be considered as a specific case of uniform multiprocessor system, the result of Funk et al. is used to provide theoretical support for the deduction of schedulability test condition.

V. NODE SCALING ALGORITHM Theorem 4.5 shows a theoretical bound for scheduling real-time tasks on a power-aware cluster. Notice that the bound can be reached only if every processor is fully utilized. For most of real-time heuristics, there are a large number of idle intervals within a feasible schedule, which means the processor utilization is less than one. In this section, we propose a Node Scaling (NS) Algorithm. NS can be applied to other real-time heuristics for further reducing power consumption. . div.head: VI. PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
div.p: In this section, we take PXA270 processor as an example, and apply NS algorithm to EDF-FF heuristic.

div.head: A. Application Example

Based on the frequency and power levels in the data sheet, the values of 𝐶 and 𝑃 𝑠 are obtained by liner regression. div.head: B. Comparison with EDF-FF
div.p: For real-time tasks over multiple processors, Lopez et al. [18] proved that no pair of uniprocessor scheduling algorithm-allocation heuristic can provide higher worsecase achievable utilization than EDF-FF. The worst-case achievable utilization is 𝑈 𝑛 = 𝛽𝑚+1 𝛽+1 , where 𝑚 is the number of processors, 𝛽 = 1/𝑢 𝑚𝑎𝑥 . For a given task set 𝜏 , we can construct a homogenous cluster at speed 𝑠 𝑚𝑎𝑥 to execute the task set without missing the timing constraints by EDF-FF heuristic. The size of cluster is easily obtained by the equation 𝑈 𝑛 = 𝛽𝑚+1 𝛽+1 . We then apply NS algorithm on EDF-FF by extending the number of processors and slowing the speed. Processor number and power consumption for the two cases are compared in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2.

Since 𝑢 𝑚𝑎𝑥 is a key element to decide the schedulability of task set as well as to decide the power-efficient speed. We vary 𝑢 𝑚𝑎𝑥 from 0.1 to 0.9, and create 2 groups of task sets with 𝑈 𝑛 = {3, 8}. From Fig. 1 and Fig. 2., NS reduces power consumption on the basis of EDF-FF by extending processor number. Besides, we find that there are linear relationships between workload 𝑈 𝑛 , processor number and power consumption. It is easy to understand that the power consumption increases with the growth in workload. If the workload 𝑈 𝑛 is fixed, processor number and power consumption also rise as 𝑢 𝑚𝑎𝑥 increases. The reason is that EDF-FF is more suitable for scheduling tasks with balanced utilization in size. These results agree well with the theoretical bound of minimum power consumption in Theorem 4.5.

In Fig. 2, the theoretical bound of power reduction in Theorem 4.5 is compared with the practical heuristics (EDF-FF and EDF-FF+NS). The power consumption of EDF-FF is much higher than NS bound. The reason is that the utilization 𝑈 𝑛 = 𝛽𝑚+1 𝛽+1 to calculate the processor number is the worst-case utilization. The tasks are scheduled according to the worst-case situation, so that processors could not be fully used to execute the tasks. Especially, the worst-case achievable utilization is proved to be 0.5(𝑛 + 1), where 𝑛 is the number of processors [18]. For an individual processor, the average utilization is 0.5(𝑛 + 1)/𝑛 ≈ 0.5, when 𝑛 is great enough. This indicates the processors spend half of the makespan to do nothing while running at the speed 𝑠 𝑚𝑎𝑥 . In contrast, minimum power consumption is obtained with assumption that processors are fully utilized. Therefore, the system power consumption of EDF-FF is approximately twice than NS bound.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: Power efficiency is an important issue to develop green datacenters. In this paper, we proposed two conditions to test whether a given task set can be scheduled over a particular cluster, and deduced a theoretical bound for power reduction. The power-efficient speed is proven to be constant for a given homogenous cluster, only depending on the type of processor. From a practical aspect, we proposed a NS algorithm applied to other heuristics, which can further reduce the energy consumption by extending the number of nodes and slowing the processor speed without missing any deadline constraints.

Since this paper is based on simple assumption of homogenous clusters, our investigation will continue considering more realistic features of datacenters. If the speed can not vary continuously, the optimization turns to be an integer programming problem. We also plan to explore NS and make it fit an uniform or a heterogenous system.
